S076-01.notes: Subject 'Katherine Dunham' (after appositive) needs a finite main verb: 'founded'. A 'founding' and B 'having founded' are nonfinite, leaving a fragment; D 'who founded' makes a relative clause, also leaving no main verb.

S076-02.notes: Singular subject 'Her time' (the intervening 'men' is a trap) takes singular past 'remained'. B 'remain' and C 'have remained' are plural; C's present perfect also clashes with 'until 1950'. D 'remaining' is nonfinite, leaving a fragment.

S076-03.notes: A plain plural is needed ('homes for ... stars'); nothing is possessed. A is singular possessive, C plural possessive, D malformed.

S076-04.notes: Teaching happened before a past event ('Before she helped start'), so past perfect 'had worked' fits. A 'has worked' (present perfect), B 'works' (present), and C 'will have worked' (future perfect) do not fit the past narrative.

S076-05.notes: The modifier 'Selected by NASA in 1990' must attach to Ochoa. In A it attaches to the shuttle, in B to Ochoa's flight (a possessive does not fix this), and in D to the flight; all three dangle.

S076-06.notes: 'however' interrupts a single clause, so it needs commas on both sides: 'remembered, however, for'. A's semicolon and D's colon would split off a dependent 'for...' phrase. C leaves the opening comma with no closing one.

S076-07.notes: Two independent clauses ('...sent a powerful stream...' / 'the moment gave him the idea'), so a semicolon is needed. A is a comma splice and B a run-on. C 'bathroom, and, the moment' puts a stray comma after 'and'.

S076-08.notes: The antecedent is the plural 'manuscripts', so 'them'. B 'it' is singular; the symphony is not described as lost, so 'it' has no fitting antecedent. C 'this' is singular and vague. D 'those ones' is nonstandard/wordy.

S076-09.notes: The appositive opens with a dash, so it must close with a dash: 'sculptures—hanging forms made of looped wire—seem'. A's comma and B's semicolon mismatch the opening dash, and B also separates subject from verb. D leaves the dash unclosed.

S076-10.notes: 'Judge distances precisely' and the contrast with touch-reliant spiders call for 'acute'. A 'blurry' and B 'limited' contradict this, and C 'ordinary' undercuts both 'remarkably' and the contrast.

S076-11.notes: The evidence (500+ performances, a major award) shows great success: 'considerable'. A 'uncertain' and C 'temporary' are contradicted. D 'predictable' has no support, and the play being a first argues against it.

S076-12.notes: The third sentence ('different mask ... ignored') is a control: it shows the response was specific to one mask. B: the passage gives no reason for wearing masks. C: the sentence supports the conclusion rather than contradicting it. D describes the first sentence.

S076-13.notes: The text explains that the ants use leaves to grow fungus rather than eating them. A: the passage makes no comparison with other species. B: 'first animals underground' is never claimed. C: the passage does not describe how the gardens were discovered.

S076-14.notes: B covers both the invention and the first-of-its-kind patent. A: the passage does not say she discovered that cataracts cause blindness. C 'replaced every other method' overstates. D: the passage mentions one patent, not many patents across medicine.

S076-15.notes: The spleen releases oxygen-rich cells, and Bajau spleens are larger, so a larger spleen may extend dives; C is suitably hedged. A and D contradict the stated mechanism. B is unsupported: the neighboring group is said not to dive.

S076-16.notes: The hypothesis needs a double touch within a short time; A contrasts 19/20 closing for close double touches with 3/20 for spaced ones, which bears directly on the timing condition. C supports only part of the hypothesis (one touch is not enough) and says nothing about the short interval, so it is weaker. B lumps the groups together and D only describes the design; neither supports the hypothesis.

S076-17.notes: Her articles called for better schools, and the League offered free classes, matching the closing link between writing and organizing. A: the passage does not mention gaining readers or wealthy families. B: nothing says she gave up journalism. C: no family decision to stop publishing in Spanish is mentioned.

S076-18.notes: Being refused lodging caused her to sleep at gas stations, so 'As a result'. A 'Nevertheless' signals contrast, C 'Similarly' signals parallel, and D 'In other words' signals restatement; none fits a cause and its effect.

S076-19.notes: The sentences move from 1968 to 1975, so 'Later' fits the sequence. A: Wimbledon is not an example of the U.S. Open win. B: the two wins do not contrast. D: the Wimbledon win does not follow logically from the earlier one.

S076-20.notes: Only D mentions materials (paper, bamboo). A gives a date, B the inspiration, and C a count.

S076-21.notes: 'Honored ... in a special election' must modify Clemente. In A it modifies the Hall of Fame, in B Clemente's induction, and in C the election; all three dangle.

S076-22.notes: Because the ants treat other nests as nestmates and do not fight, connected nests can merge into a supercolony, so 'As a result' fits. A 'Nevertheless' and B 'In contrast' wrongly signal opposition. D 'Similarly' is wrong because the supercolony is a consequence of the behavior, not a parallel case. The second sentence reads partly like an illustration, but no example transition is offered, so C is clearly best.
